hints: Notice the three blocks from left to right: 1 resistor alone, then 2 resistors in parallel, then 3 resistors in parallel, all joined in series.
Recall that series resistances add, while for $n$ equal resistors $R$ in parallel the combined resistance is $R/n$.
Write the total as $R + R/2 + R/3 = 66\text{ k}\Omega$ and solve for $R$.
walkthrough: Split the diagram into three series sections: the single $R$ on the left, the middle block of two $R$ in parallel, and the right block of three $R$ in parallel.
For resistors in series, $R_{total} = R_1 + R_2 + ...$. For resistors in parallel, $1/R_p = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2 + ...$.
Add the three sections in series: $R_{combined} = R + R/2 + R/3 = (6R + 3R + 2R)/6 = 11R/6$.
Set equal to the given total: $11R/6 = 66\text{ k}\Omega$, so $R = 66\text{ k}\Omega \times 6/11 = 36\text{ k}\Omega$.

options.A: Dividing $66\text{ k}\Omega$ by 6 treats all six $R$ resistors as in series, ignoring the two parallel groups.
options.B: This value does not satisfy $R + R/2 + R/3 = 66\text{ k}\Omega$ for the one-series plus two-parallel plus three-parallel arrangement.
options.C: This value would give a total of $40.3\text{ k}\Omega$, because the two-resistor and three-resistor parallel groups have resistance less than $R$.
